chunks: From him, from Abū Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: Whoever coughs up phlegm in the mosque and then returns it into his body, it will not pass by any illness within his body except that it cures him from it.

key_terms.أَبْرَأَتْهُ: it cured him or restored him to health
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the sacred place of worship
key_terms.تَنَخَّعَ: to cough up or expel phlegm
key_terms.جَوْفِهِ: his interior or inside his body

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about expelling phlegm in the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches conduct connected to the sanctity of the mosque and discourages spitting or expelling phlegm in it. It also mentions a bodily benefit for one who restrains himself in this setting, linking mosque etiquette with personal well-being.
